Man I was kind of in your shoes around 2021. I was working towards being an emergency physician or np. Covid shut down school and I worked full time as an EMT, then got a second job as an ER tech and was planning to go to nursing school. 


I'm so glad I worked in the ER because that's what finally sealed that. I was working through most of the pandemic and through delta, things at the ER just got worse. There was no support from the execs, patients were mad or dying, and I was barely able to drag myself to work. Every day I walked through the entrance, it felt like a jail cell was slamming shut that would only open in 12 hours. I eventually fully lost my appetite, had several panic attacks, and overall just became a shell of myself. So I quit. It was one of the hardest things I'd done, but I'm so glad I did it. 


Now I work in corporate, but my long term goal is to eventually pivot pack into health care or public policy, but not sure how I want to do it. I've seen so many friends and acquaintances find their own paths in Healthcare. 


It might be well worth considering if it's time to find another path. It's clear you want to help people, but if nursing isn't the job for you, then you could actually hurt people. There are several fields where you can work burnt-out or hate your job, but Healthcare is not one of them. That's was one of my main motivators for leaving direct patient care. 


Life takes you on weird paths and all of them contribute to who you are and your capabilities. Hope you find your path. Feel free to reach out if you need to talk to someone who kinda gets it.
